# Can Make Arithmetic Progression From Sequence.

@example In the order -2, 4, 10 each number is 6 more than the one before.
[10,-2,4]
=> true

@example Any such order would have to put 2 between 0 and 6, but 2 is not halfway between them.
[0,6,2]
=> false

@example Three equal values work with the step d = 0.
[8,8,8]
=> true

# Two numbers can always be lined up, even the two extremes.
[1000000,-1000000]
=> true

# Two equal numbers.
[-7,-7]
=> true

# 1, 3, 5, 7 with the 5 replaced by a second 3.
[1,3,3,7]
=> false

# The smallest, the largest and the sum are those of 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, and
# every value is one of those five, but 4 occurs three times.
[4,8,4,0,4]
=> false

# The same trap with two pairs: 0, 1, 2, 3 has the same ends and sum.
[0,0,3,3]
=> false

# The range 7 does not split into 3 equal gaps.
[0,7,3,5]
=> false

# The step would be 3 (2, 5, 8, 11), but 9 sits between two places.
[2,11,5,9]
=> false

# Already in decreasing order, crossing zero.
[12,9,6,3,0,-3]
=> true

# Shuffled, with step 5 across negative and positive values.
[15,-5,5,0,10,20,-10]
=> true

# Sorted, only the last gap is different.
[6,3,1,4,2]
=> false

# Sorted, only the first gap is different.
[5,0,3,4,2]
=> false

# Gaps of 1 and 65537, which agree only in their low 16 bits.
[65541,3,4]
=> false

# The whole range of values, in steps of 500000.
[500000,-1000000,1000000,0,-500000]
=> true

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 3 small
[6,8,-2,0,-4,9,4,2]
=> false

@gen 9 small
[-3,-5,-5,-5,-7,-8,-9]
=> false

@gen 10 small
[-1,-3,-5,1,7,5,3,-7]
=> true

@gen 14 small
[1,-4,-2]
=> false

@gen 23 small
[1,4,3,2,5,7,8,6]
=> true

@gen 28 small
[0,-3,9,3,-6,6]
=> true

@gen 37 small
[-3,-2,-1,-1,1,2]
=> false
